# Introduction

Mechanistic interpretability increasingly studies whether language models
*plan*: whether internal representations of future content causally shape
earlier tokens that license that content [@hanna2026latent]. On
article--noun tasks such as choosing \(a\) versus \(an\) before an
occupation noun, dual-effect sparse features that affect both article
logits and future-noun attributions look like planning features. Under
free generation, intervening on them can flip `a pilot` into
`an aviator`. But this observation does not identify whether a latent state
persists independently into noun computation.

We call the ambiguity **generated-token mediation**. Once an intervention
changes article \(b\), ordinary autoregressive decoding opens the path
\(I\to b\to c\): the sampled article becomes part of the visible prefix
used to predict noun \(c\). This does not make direct persistence
architecturally impossible---later positions can attend to earlier residual
states---but it makes free-generation evidence non-identifying. The required
test is a factorial intervention that crosses \(I\in\{0,1\}\) with
\(b\in\{\text{free},\operatorname{do}(a),\operatorname{do}(an)\}\), keeps
\(I\) active during noun prediction, and compares noun distributions under
an identical token prefix.

**Contributions.** On pretrained Gemma~3 270M with Gemma Scope~2 affine
cross-layer transcoders [@gemmascope2; @hanna2025circuittracer], we:

1. Separate three accounts: modular editable planning (**H1**), fused
   article--noun packages (**H2**), and article control plus autoregressive
   continuation (**H3**).
2. Run the exact S1-by-article factorial on all 20 pre-specified held-out
   prompts. Article insertion alone reproduces the S1-on top-1 noun on
   20/20 prompts; on the 19 article-switching prompts, same-prefix residual
   variation is \(0.029\) versus total variation \(0.940\).
3. Detect a small but nonzero token-clamped residual on seven pre-specified
   twins under fixed `an` (\(+0.089\) logits, 95\% bootstrap interval
   \([0.027,0.152]\)), distinguishing *overwhelmingly mediated* from
   *no direct effect*.
4. Verify that S1 perturbations propagate from the pre-article position into
   later article-position features, and validate noun-assay sensitivity with
   a development-selected full-residual reference on held-out pairs.

Our contribution is not a claim that latent planning is absent. It is an
identification result: a large free-generation intervention effect can be
almost completely recreated by the generated mediator token, while a much
smaller token-clamped residual remains. This decomposition is a reusable
standard for claims of persistent latent control in autoregressive models.
